title: Invertibility of normalized affine cohomology edge components
statement: Let A and B be commutative rings, phi : B → A, i an integer, and assume the sheaf derived categories [def-pc-derived-category]. Put T_R = tilde and f = Spec(phi). Fix an ordinary comparison isomorphism sigma : res_phi ⋙ T_B ≅ T_A ⋙ f_*. Define q_(C,i) and b_(C,t) by the explicit derived-unit and tilde-cohomology-coordinate composites of [def-pc-derived-direct-image] and [def-pc-affine-base-change-tilde-coordinates], using sigma as the termwise comparison. Let alpha be any natural transformation T_B res_phi Gamma_A H^i → H^i Rf_* on D_QCoh(Spec A) [lem-pc-affine-derived-cohomology-presentation]. Assume q_(C,i) followed by H^i(Rf_*t) equals T_B res_phi(b_(C,t)) followed by alpha_L whenever C is an unbounded A-module complex and t : Q(T_A C) ≅ L has hom equal to eqToHom of an object equality. Then alpha_L is an isomorphism for every L. This is an invertibility implication, not an existence statement.

source.place: perfect.tex, lemma-affine-morphism-equivalence, cohomology display; lemma-application-nice-K-injective, bound-one truncation; affine derived equivalence (06Z0).

proof.text: Choose a K-injective resolution of the termwise tilde complex. Affine pushforward of this resolution is a quasi-isomorphism by lem-pc-affine-pushforward-resolution-quasi-iso. Naturality of the actual right-derived unit and its invertibility on K-injective complexes make that unit invertible on the tilde complex. All other factors in the defined comparison q are images of isomorphisms, hence q is invertible.
At the identity representative the assumed normalization writes q as T_B res_phi(b) followed by alpha. The first factor is an isomorphism, hence alpha at Q(T_A C) is an isomorphism.

The affine derived equivalence (06Z0) represents every L by some Q(T_A C). Naturality of alpha along that representative isomorphism writes alpha_L as a composite of the invertible representative component and two functor images of an isomorphism. Therefore alpha_L is invertible.

proof_origin.place: Affine resolution comparison, right-derived-unit naturality, and affine derived representatives.
proof_origin.note: Use the actual resolution map instead of an unnormalized abstract cohomology isomorphism.

theorem affinePushforwardCohomologyEdge_isIso
    (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] (φ : B →+* A) (i : ℤ)
    (σ : ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ ⋙ affinePushforwardTilde B ≅
      affinePushforwardTilde A ⋙
        Scheme.Modules.pushforward (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))) :
  ∀ (α : affineDerivedCohomologyModules A i ⋙
      (ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ ⋙ affinePushforwardTilde B) ⟶
    (schemeDerivedQCohProperty (Spec (.of A))).ι ⋙
      schemeDerivedDirectImage (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ)) ⋙
      DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (Spec (.of B)).toRingedSpace)) i),
    (∀ (C : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
      (L : schemeDerivedQCohCategory (Spec (.of A)))
      (t : DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (((affinePushforwardTilde A).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj C) ≅ L.obj),
      (∃ h : DerivedCategory.Q.obj
          (((affinePushforwardTilde A).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj C) = L.obj,
        t.hom = eqToHom h) →
      affinePushforwardCohomologyMapOfComparison A B φ σ C i ≫
        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (Spec (.of B)).toRingedSpace)) i).map
          ((schemeDerivedDirectImage (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom φ))).map t.hom) =
        (affinePushforwardTilde B).map ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars φ).map
          (affinePushforwardRepresentativeCohomologyIso A C L.obj t i).hom) ≫ α.app L) →
    ∀ L, IsIso (α.app L)
